page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 208.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per core, and includes 1229 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory operations. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1822.89 and a multi-core score of 57247.25. Memory bandwidth tests show 2231.95 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, 170.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 77.64 GB/sec for large-block writes. In database and web serving tests, the instance processed 41.96 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a static web serving throughput of 32.4 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs are evident in single-core and text processing tasks, where Geekbench scores of 1122.0 and 1428.0 are categorized as weak. Large-scale language model inference is also a bottleneck, with 70B model prompt processing and text generation scoring in the poor range at 3.6 and 2.43 tokens per second, respectively. However, the server demonstrates average efficiency for software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and web serving that benefit from dedicated ARM cores and local storage, rather than heavy single-threaded processing or large-scale AI inference.
